recommendations.item: Vodka rigatoni (where he first tried it)
recommendations.reason: The Italian-American restaurant where he first had the spicy, creamy tomato pasta that became his main.
recommendations.quote: the first time I had it was in this restaurant in America called Carbone
recommendations.speaker: Ed Sheeran

recommendations.item: Bowl of fat-cut fried chips
recommendations.reason: Not too chunky and not triple-cooked, for mopping up the vodka rigatoni sauce.
recommendations.quote: Just a bowl of chips and then if it's the vodka rigatoni, you soak it up with the chips.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Sheeran

recommendations.item: A bottle of red Burgundy followed by a bottle of Bordeaux
recommendations.reason: A red-wine lover who did a sommelier course, he marks every achievement with a signed and dated bottle.
recommendations.quote: I'd start off with a bottle of Burgundy and move to a bottle of Bordeaux.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Sheeran

recommendations.item: Pint of draught Asahi in a frosted glass, before the meal
recommendations.reason: He thinks Asahi is the best beer and the first pint is always the best. He even keeps a freezer of frosted glasses in his garden pub.
recommendations.quote: Asahi from Japan but, yes, it has to be on tap. It has to be on tap.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Sheeran

recommendations.item: Apple strudel
recommendations.reason: He wavered between tarte tatin, Hard Rock Cafe profiteroles and strudel, then settled on apple strudel.
recommendations.quote: Yes I'd go for the apple-, can I just say strudel? Apple strudel.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Sheeran

recommendations.item: Extra-hot chicken wrap and coleslaw
recommendations.reason: His lunch every single day when doing promo in London; he has a Nando's Black Card.
recommendations.quote: If I'm doing promo, it's always an extra hot chicken wrap and a coleslaw, every time.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Sheeran

recommendations.item: Three-Michelin-star dining
recommendations.reason: He goes often and takes people there when he wants a really nice evening.
recommendations.quote: there's a restaurant in the West called Core that I go to a lot that has three stars
recommendations.speaker: Ed Sheeran

recommendations.item: Demi-brioche burger buns
recommendations.reason: Ed Gamble recommends its half-sweet demi-brioche bun, and Sheeran enjoyed its lockdown burger kit.
recommendations.quote: It's a demi-brioche. It's half sweet, it's perfect. It's just what you need.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

recommendations.item: Restaurant visits on tour
recommendations.reason: His security guard and manager love it, so they've ended up at Hard Rocks in Japan and Ushuaia. He'd have a profiterole or a big chocolate dessert there.
recommendations.quote: we love it so much that we just end up there.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Sheeran

episodes.title: Ep 126: Jack Dee
episodes.summary: Jack Dee's French-brasserie dream meal: sparkling Perrier, ciabatta or focaccia, grilled oysters, confit duck, sauteed cubed potatoes with lardons plus slow-cooked green beans, 'booze' (ideally beer), and his mum's hazelnut meringue roulade with raspberry coulis and vanilla ice cream.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water (small cans of Perrier)
recommendations.reason: Sparkling water cures his heartburn, so he stashes small cans of very fizzy Perrier everywhere.
recommendations.quote: I like a sparkling water because it's good for your digestion. I've had very bad heartburn in the past
recommendations.speaker: Jack Dee

recommendations.item: Ciabatta or focaccia
recommendations.reason: He likes proper bread, ciabatta being his favourite; he gave up baking his own and prefers supporting a nice local baker.
recommendations.quote: I like proper bread. I love ciabatta, it's probably my favourite. Or possibly a focaccia sometimes
recommendations.speaker: Jack Dee

recommendations.item: Grilled oysters with breadcrumbs, garlic, chorizo or spinach (plus a couple raw)
recommendations.reason: A compromise he and his wife Jane came up with - lightly grilled oysters with toppings, done at the table himself.
recommendations.quote: you can grill the oysters with a delicious bit of-, you know, little bits and pieces on top of it.
recommendations.speaker: Jack Dee

recommendations.item: Confit duck
recommendations.reason: His favourite dish - slow-cooked, tender and melt-in-the-mouth; he often serves good jarred versions from a nice food shop at home.
recommendations.quote: my favourite dish, probably, is confit duck... Very slow and tender. It's incredibly tender.
recommendations.speaker: Jack Dee

recommendations.item: Cubed potatoes sauteed with lardons (pommes parmentier), plus French-style slow-cooked buttery green beans
recommendations.reason: A classic French brasserie side, like mini roast potatoes with lardon flavour; the hosts added his beloved soft buttery green beans too.
recommendations.quote: they're sautéed with lardons. Like little, mini roast potatoes and they're beautiful
recommendations.speaker: Jack Dee

recommendations.item: Booze - ideally beer (real ale or artisan lager)
recommendations.reason: He'd love to just ask a sommelier for 'booze'; he likes beer-coloured booze, no novelty colours.
recommendations.quote: I'd ask for booze. I'd love to do that to a sommelier. 'Can I have some booze please?'
recommendations.speaker: Jack Dee

recommendations.item: Hazelnut meringue roulade with whipped cream, raspberry coulis and vanilla ice cream
recommendations.venue: His mum's (now made by his wife Jane)
recommendations.reason: Hazelnut is his favourite flavour and his mum used to make this roulade; Jane now makes it better than he does.
recommendations.quote: hazelnut meringue in a roulade... That to me is a complete perfection... My mum used to make that
recommendations.speaker: Jack Dee

recommendations.item: Confit duck
recommendations.reason: Ed's wife lived above this Marais bistro, which did amazing confit duck and had the owners' bulldog roaming around.
recommendations.quote: it was a bistro restaurant. They did amazing confit duck but it was called Bulldog
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

episodes.title: Ep 127: Timothy Spall
episodes.summary: Timothy Spall picks an imperial gallon of diet cloudy lemonade, a mezze of ramekins and Padrón peppers, his wife's oxtail stew with fluffy potatoes and Mother's Pride to mop up, and Notarianni's ice cream with a banana split and cheeseboard.

recommendations.item: Diet cloudy lemonade (by the imperial gallon) - otherwise sparkling water with a little jug of Rose's lime cordial
recommendations.reason: A self-described 'cloudy lemonade-drinking fish', he is allowed his beloved diet cloudy lemonade as his water.
recommendations.quote: I do love that and that would be on the desert island, I think. I'd have to have that in a well.
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: Spicy and plain poppadoms with relish tray, Spanish crusty bread with oil and balsamic
recommendations.reason: He loves both and wants the airy, dark-crusted Spanish bread and the full relish tray with lime pickle and mango chutney.
recommendations.quote: you know that bread you get in Spain will all the air holes in but it's soft and it's got a dark crust on it? I love that.
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: His wife's homemade focaccia
recommendations.reason: His wife became a master baker in lockdown and her focaccia rivals the best they've had in Italy.
recommendations.quote: She makes this focaccia, and we've been to Italy quite a lot and honestly it's up there with the best.
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: Mezze: ramekins of plain crisps with cheese cubes, peanuts, olives, Marmite crispbreads; deep-fried baby artichoke; fish goujons; Padrón peppers
recommendations.location: Rome, Italy (where he first had the deep-fried artichoke)
recommendations.reason: A nibbly tapas spread; he discovered the tiny deep-fried artichoke at a place in Rome and adores a beer-battered goujon.
recommendations.quote: We were recently in Rome and we went to this place and I had something I never had before which was a deep fried small artichoke.
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: Oxtail stew, finished with a little tandoori chicken / chicken shashlik
recommendations.reason: His wife of 40 years told him oxtail is what he really likes; she cooks it into a dark, medieval, falling-apart stew.
recommendations.quote: this amazing, sort of, vat, like a huge bowl of meaty, kind of dark, almost medieval-type thing comes out with this beautiful, soft meat
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: Over-boiled fluffy potatoes, crispy roast potatoes, tinned marrowfat peas, nine fat chips, and Mother's Pride white bread to soak up the gravy
recommendations.reason: Fluffy potatoes like his nan made to absorb the sauce, and white bread soaked in oxtail gravy recalling childhood plate-licking.
recommendations.quote: Oxtail juice soaked Mother's Pride. There. And you eat it delicately and with precision, with a knife and fork.
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: M&S fizzy cranberry lemonade and boiling-hot Robinson's apple and blackcurrant with lemon
recommendations.reason: Having given up wine, these soft drinks are now his delights and evening reward.
recommendations.quote: I'd probably be able to get another, maybe a Marks & Spencers fizzy cranberry lemonade down. I really like them
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: Old-fashioned vanilla and chocolate ice cream
recommendations.location: Battersea, London, UK (ice cream made at the bottom of Battersea Park Road, sold from vans around Lavender Hill)
recommendations.reason: Childhood memory of running out after Sunday lunch with the biggest dessert bowl to get Mr Notarianni's Italian ice cream from the van.
recommendations.quote: There was Notarianni's, which was the Italian, old-fashioned ice cream, made down the bottom of Battersea Park Road
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: Banana split with chocolate sauce, followed by a cheeseboard (Brie de Meaux, Colston Bassett stilton, gorgonzola) with Jacob's cream crackers
recommendations.reason: The banana split reminds him of childhood seaside trips to Margate; later he discovered great cheeses.
recommendations.quote: because it reminds me of going to the seaside, down to Margate as a kid, I think I'll have a banana split.
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

recommendations.item: Triple-cooked chips
recommendations.reason: He had Heston Blumenthal's triple-cooked chips there once and found them delicious, if a little overdone for his taste.
recommendations.quote: I did go there and have them, they were absolutely delicious at 'The Fat Duck'. Only the once, it was delightful
recommendations.speaker: Timothy Spall

episodes.title: Ep 128: Miquita Oliver
episodes.summary: Broadcaster Miquita Oliver goes deliberately plain: still Brita water, nutty brown bread, a bitter-leaf salad with her family's champagne oysters, mince and tatties with peas, cauliflower cheese and carrots, a big glass of Syrah and apple crumble with jugs of cold single cream.

recommendations.item: Very cold still water from a Brita filter
recommendations.reason: She distrusts sparkling water and hates tap water; her tenner Brita jug from Argos makes cold filtered water she drinks all day.
recommendations.quote: What I got, James, is a Brita water filter from Argos for a tenner which is the best tenner I ever spent.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Warm nutty brown bread in hunks with home-made butter
recommendations.reason: The kind of crusty-outside, soft-inside brown bread served in nice West London restaurants when she was growing up.
recommendations.quote: that really nice, nutty, warm, brown bread that comes in, like, really quite nice restaurants. With their, like, home-made butter.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Green leaf salad (radicchio, parsley, dandelion, watercress, sorrel) with the Oliver family oysters - hot sauce, shallot vinegar and a shot of champagne
recommendations.reason: A family recipe (also her mum Andi's starter): oysters with hot sauce, shallot vinegar and champagne that she calls a 'livener' before a meal.
recommendations.quote: it is just oysters with hot sauce, shallot vinegar, and then the pièce de résistance, a shot of champagne.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Mince and tatties with white whipped mash, peas and creamy mushroom gravy
recommendations.reason: Her Scottish dad first made it for her aged eight in a squat in south London and it made her feel loved and safe.
recommendations.quote: he made me mince and tatties and I felt really loved and safe, and he really knows how to make mashed potato.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Cauliflower cheese and carrots
recommendations.reason: She loves cauliflower cheese and needs carrots for some orange among the white and brown.
recommendations.quote: If I'm having cauliflower cheese then I have to have carrots because I need that orange to deal with all the white and brown.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Big glass of Syrah red wine
recommendations.reason: Through her wine podcast she learned she likes dark, full-bodied 'chestnutty' wine, i.e. Syrah.
recommendations.quote: I like a very dark, full-body, chestnutty wine which is, as my lovely co-presenter has told me, a Syrah.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Hot apple crumble with sultanas and jugs of cold single cream
recommendations.reason: Classic comforting English pudding; she wants far more cold single cream than restaurants give.
recommendations.quote: Apple crumble. Cold single cream. The crumble has to be hot and I like it to have sultanas in it
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Old-school caff with green and white tiles
recommendations.location: City Road, Old Street, London, UK
recommendations.reason: Her model for the dream restaurant's look: a good old-school caff that looks like a pie and mash shop.
recommendations.quote: There was a caf called The Shepherdess on Old Street on the corner and it was, like, sort of, green and white tiled.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Aligot-style cheesy mashed potato
recommendations.location: Old Compton Street, Soho, London, UK
recommendations.reason: She went to the late-night Soho spot for its great mashed potato.
recommendations.quote: I think it was Balans used to have that in Soho. I was there for very different reasons than other people. I was there for the potatoes.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

recommendations.item: Mince on toast with watercress
recommendations.reason: One of Ed's favourite London restaurants; its mince on toast is 'the best mince you'll ever taste' and his first meal there after lockdown gave him goosebumps.
recommendations.quote: It's one of my favourite restaurants in London and they do a dish which... it's mince on toast and it's just the best mince you'll ever taste
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

recommendations.item: Gastropub food
recommendations.reason: Miquita calls it the first ever gastropub with brilliant food, though a bit rich for her.
recommendations.quote: it's opposite the Eagle isn't it, which was, like, the first ever gastropub, which is bloody brilliant food but a bit too rich for me.
recommendations.speaker: Miquita Oliver

episodes.title: Ep 129: Jason Reitman
episodes.summary: Jason Reitman, who says he hates home cooking, chooses sparkling water, poppadoms he's never tried, White Bear's spicy dumplings in Flushing, Charlie's Back Door's green chile enchilada fried as tempura by a Tokyo chef, a City Bakery pretzel croissant plus a dilly dog, Shokunin's smoked Old Fashioned and his grandmother's kugelhopf.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water
recommendations.reason: He doesn't really like water, but sparkling is delicious and an experience, and he can't imagine choosing still unless he'd just been running.
recommendations.quote: It's delicious. It's an experience. I also don't like water.
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

recommendations.item: Poppadoms with chutney (never tried before)
recommendations.reason: Having never heard of poppadoms, he picks them after the hosts describe them, wanting to be the guest who tries new things.
recommendations.quote: Well, I want what you just described. Poppadoms, please.
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

recommendations.item: Spicy dumplings
recommendations.reason: A tiny family-run stand that only really makes one dish and serves until it runs out; the soft, spicy dumplings have a taste he's never had anywhere else and he fantasises about going back.
recommendations.quote: they have these little spicy dumplings. It's the only thing they have on the menu and I fantasise about them.
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

recommendations.item: Green chile sour cream enchilada
recommendations.reason: A now-closed, dark strip-mall dive bar with year-round Christmas decorations whose soupy, sloppy green chile enchilada was phenomenal; it breaks his heart he can't go back.
recommendations.quote: particularly my favourite dish which was their green chilli, sour cream, enchilada, which sounds awful, but was phenomenal, and it breaks my heart that I can't go back.
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

recommendations.item: Omakase tempura cooked in front of you (the chef dips the enchilada in tempura batter in the dream version)
recommendations.reason: A tiny, hard-to-find counter where the chef dips item after item in batter and you just eat what he gives you, making your own dipping sauce; light and heavy at once and pure experience start to finish.
recommendations.quote: So, in Tokyo, there is a restaurant called Mikawa and it's a tiny place in a suburban neighbourhood that is hard to find
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

recommendations.item: Pretzel croissant
recommendations.reason: A dry, crumbly, salty, sesame-topped croissant he loves; the LA branch closed so he has to go to New York for one.
recommendations.quote: It's dry. It just crumbles in your hand and it's salty and it's delicious.
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

recommendations.item: Dilly dog (hot dog in a pickle, deep fried like a corn dog, with mustard)
recommendations.reason: His favourite item from a Major League Baseball 'Frankenfood' event showcasing ballpark foods; James likes it so much he adds it as a bonus dish.
recommendations.quote: There was one that was a hot dog wrapped in a pickle then deep fried like a corn dog and then mustard sprayed on it.
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

recommendations.item: Smoked Old Fashioned rolled in a smoke-filled glass sphere
recommendations.reason: Calgary is an amazing food town and Shokunin gave him one of the best Japanese meals of his life; its theatrical smoked Old Fashioned is the best he's had.
recommendations.quote: And it's delicious. It's the best Old Fashioned I've ever had.
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

recommendations.item: Kugelhopf (Hungarian marbled chocolate bread-cake)
recommendations.reason: His grandmother always served it, so he associates it with her; the bread tastes like bread and the chocolate is the richest he's had, and nothing elsewhere matches it.
recommendations.quote: it's a Hungarian pastry called kugelhopf and I have found it nowhere else but in Toronto where my family is from
recommendations.speaker: Jason Reitman

episodes.title: Ep 130: Bridget Christie
episodes.summary: Bridget Christie's family-centred dream menu: still water, a lick of Last Supper wine, hospital tea and toast, her daughter's mackerel tart with 1980s salad, pesto linguine in Sardinia, her dad Pete's potatoes, ten lavender cocktails from the Soho Hotel and her late mum's apple pie with rose goats' milk ice cream from Mirepoix.

recommendations.item: Still water
recommendations.reason: Can't do sparkling: it's too gassy and sticks in her tight throat. Also calls water her favourite drink overall.
recommendations.quote: Oh God, still every time, can't do sparkling. (a) it's very gassy, gaseous
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Hot buttered white toast and a cup of builders' tea given by a midwife after giving birth
recommendations.reason: Swapped in for her original poppadoms choice; the simple kindness of tea and toast after giving birth felt profound and moving.
recommendations.quote: just a cup of tea and a piece of toast. So simple, but yet so meaningful and so welcomed, and so needed, and so kind.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Poppadoms (original choice, later swapped for tea and toast)
recommendations.reason: Picked over bread because bread makes her too full and gives her cramps.
recommendations.quote: Bread, be too full and also I have, like, a wheat, I don't know what I've got.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Daughter's smoked mackerel, leek and pea tart with 1980s salad (butterhead lettuce, salad cream) and spinach
recommendations.reason: Her ten-year-old daughter makes it properly with homemade shortcrust pastry; the salad evokes summers at her dad's house when salad tasted more vibrant.
recommendations.quote: can I have please, my daughter's mackerel tart? With salad from the 1980s.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Linguine with fresh pesto and pine nuts
recommendations.reason: A simple pasta dish on a windy day by a beach in Sardinia, with her toddler daughter asleep on her; she has never had anything like it since.
recommendations.quote: it was pasta with fresh pesto and pine nuts and whatever they did with it, I don't know, but I've never had anything like it before or since.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Dad Pete's chips/roast potatoes
recommendations.reason: Her dad's potatoes are famous in the family: light inside, hard and crunchy outside, the perfect colour every time.
recommendations.quote: No one who's come to the house, he's been in that house since the late 50s, has ever had a potato cooked better than how my dad has cooked them.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Lavender cocktail with egg white (ten small glasses)
recommendations.reason: So good she had six or seven of the tiny cocktails; very lavender-y with lavender on top.
recommendations.quote: It was at Soho Hotel... It was in a tiny little glass and it had lavender on the top and it was very lavender-y. God it was so good.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: The aromatised wine Jesus drank at the Last Supper (a lick, as an aperitif)
recommendations.reason: Raised Catholic with a gold Last Supper sculpture at home; she'd love a tiny taste of the original wine, untreated.
recommendations.quote: The wine that Jesus gave his disciples, at the Last Supper.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Mum's apple pie
recommendations.reason: Her mum, who died in 1997, was a great baker; homemade apple pie takes her straight back to her childhood kitchen.
recommendations.quote: Home-made apple pie, to me, is my mum... I'd be right back to my kitchen when I was little, and her with her wooden spoon and her cardigan
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Rose goats' milk ice cream (in a separate bowl)
recommendations.venue: Goats' milk ice cream van (Mirepoix market)
recommendations.reason: A van from a nearby farm in the medieval market town; the family would drive two hours just for the delicately flavoured rose ice cream and still talk about it.
recommendations.quote: This little town, market town, used to have an ice-cream van, which was from a farm which was about 25km away, that used goats' milk for its ice- cream.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Filter coffee with non-dairy milk
recommendations.reason: Wanted to end the meal with a filter coffee, which she complains you can't get anywhere.
recommendations.quote: Could I have a filter coffee, please, which you cannot get anywhere. Drives me bloody mental.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

recommendations.item: Family holiday camp
recommendations.reason: Where her family holidayed every year, near Mirepoix and the rose ice cream.
recommendations.quote: We always, every year, used to go on holiday... to a little French holiday camp place called Domaine de L'Esplanade, which is in Quillan.
recommendations.speaker: Bridget Christie

episodes.title: Ep 131: Sarah Kendall (Christmas Special)
episodes.summary: Sarah Kendall's dessert-averse Christmas menu: two starters (beef carpaccio and Edinburgh Fringe oysters), Hvar lobster tail spaghetti with Chinatown roast duck, a cheeseboard and a 'spider' Coke float.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water
recommendations.reason: She drinks about 800ml of SodaStream sparkling water a day, especially while fasting.
recommendations.quote: Sparkling, I'll go sparkling, please.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Six-ounce oat milk flat white
recommendations.reason: A self-confessed coffee snob, she wants to start with a small, strong, not-too-milky flat white.
recommendations.quote: I'm six-ounce oat milk flat white, so I've already been a bit of a prick about it
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: The crusty heel of a sourdough loaf
recommendations.reason: She doesn't want to fill up on bread, so just a crusty corner of sourdough.
recommendations.quote: Yes, a corner of sourdough, really crusty.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Beef carpaccio with olive oil, baby capers, parmesan and rocket
recommendations.reason: She loves cured and thinly sliced meats and prefers small, flavour-packed starters to mains.
recommendations.quote: I really like, like, cured meat, so I like a carpaccio anything.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Nine oysters with lemon, salt and Tabasco
recommendations.venue: Oyster sellers at the Pleasance Courtyard
recommendations.reason: Kilted brothers selling West Coast oysters at the Edinburgh Fringe gave her the best oysters of her life.
recommendations.quote: They were the best oysters I've ever had in my life.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Lobster tail spaghetti
recommendations.reason: Her happiest meal ever, eaten on a hot night in a beautiful Venetian-built cobbled town in Hvar.
recommendations.quote: I had a lobster tail spaghetti in Hvar and everything was just perfect that night.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Roast fatty duck
recommendations.reason: She loves fatty meats she can't cook at home; she had an exceptional roast duck in Chinatown the night before.
recommendations.quote: it's roast duck. Like, I had one last night in Chinatown and it was just exceptional.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Cheeseboard with adult blue cheeses, quince and savoury biscuits
recommendations.reason: She thinks dessert is for babies and prefers savoury cheese.
recommendations.quote: I want savoury biscuits with it too. I want savoury. Savoury biscuits, some quince and some adult cheese.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: A 'spider' (Coca-Cola with ice cream)
recommendations.reason: She loves full-fat Coca-Cola and turns it into a spider, the Coke float she grew up with in Australia.
recommendations.quote: in Australia, when I was growing up, a spider was a Coca-Cola with ice cream in it.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Ice-cold Coopers Pale Ale
recommendations.reason: She only drinks for the ceremony of a really cold beer, and if pushed would pick the Aussie Coopers Pale Ale.
recommendations.quote: I'll say a Coopers Pale Ale. I do like Coopers. It's an Aussie beer
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Christmas seafood barbecue (snapper, oysters, prawns)
recommendations.reason: Her favourite Christmas is the Australian summer seafood cook-up with fish-market snapper on the barbie.
recommendations.quote: we'd go to the fish markets, get a really big snapper, put that on the barbie, get oysters, prawns.
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: British-style gastropub
recommendations.reason: The English-style pub she worked at during university, serving roasts and Newcastle Brown Ale, which she says was really good.
recommendations.quote: it was actually a really good restaurant, but as I say, I just didn't have the people skills
recommendations.speaker: Sarah Kendall

recommendations.item: Off Menu Christmas pizza and Marmite cheese garlic bread
recommendations.reason: The hosts plug their Christmas collaboration pizza with pigs in blankets and crispy sprouts at Yard Sale.
recommendations.quote: I had it last night, James, it was absolutely fantastic.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

episodes.title: Ep 132: Harry Hill (Christmas Special)
episodes.summary: Harry Hill's classic, cream-loving menu: still water, focaccia with olive oil, potted shrimp on toast, spaghetti vongole, roast turkey with devils on horseback for Christmas, mange tout for the joke, Gavi di Gavi and trifle.

recommendations.item: Still water, no ripples
recommendations.reason: He wants water so still it has no ripples, joking about chaos theory.
recommendations.quote: Still water. I'm saying still water, really still.
recommendations.speaker: Harry Hill

recommendations.item: Focaccia with olive oil
recommendations.reason: He likes elastic, oily bread with just olive oil, finding balsamic too sweet; he baked focaccia in lockdown.
recommendations.quote: I like a bread that is, sort of, elastic-y and oily.
recommendations.speaker: Harry Hill

recommendations.item: Potted shrimp with warm toast
recommendations.reason: Shrimps set in hard nutmeggy butter, spread on hot toast; he went shrimping as a child in Eastbourne and cites Morecambe Bay as the classic.
recommendations.quote: Hard cold butter that's got, like, a nutmeg-y flavour to it.
recommendations.speaker: Harry Hill

recommendations.item: Spaghetti vongole ('spag-vong')
recommendations.reason: Spaghetti with baby clams in an oily, garlicky sauce with a little tomato.
recommendations.quote: The mains, I'm going for spag-vong, spaghetti vongole.
recommendations.speaker: Harry Hill

recommendations.item: Christmas dinner: roast turkey with all the trimmings plus devils on horseback with mango chutney
recommendations.reason: He cooks and carves a turkey supplied by his organic farmer brother, roasted upside down, with goose-fat potatoes and devils on horseback.
recommendations.quote: Prunes wrapped in bacon, with a bit of mango chutney in the middle of the prune.
recommendations.speaker: Harry Hill

recommendations.item: Mange tout (for the joke)
recommendations.reason: Chosen mainly so he can do his old 'couldn't eat a whole one' joke; he finds them a bit stringy.
recommendations.quote: I like the mange tout, but I couldn't eat a whole one, is a joke.
recommendations.speaker: Harry Hill

recommendations.item: Gavi di Gavi
recommendations.reason: A crisp Italian white that goes with the seafood meal.
recommendations.quote: a glass or a bottle of Gavi di Gavi, the Italian wine. A crisp white wine.
recommendations.speaker: Harry Hill

recommendations.item: Trifle
recommendations.reason: He loves cream in all its forms rather than very sweet things, so picks trifle.
recommendations.quote: I like creamy things, cream in all its forms, pouring cream, double cream, whipped cream, clotted cream
recommendations.speaker: Harry Hill

episodes.title: Ep 133: Tim Key
episodes.summary: Tim Key goes for a curry-house-style feast with a water wheel of tap water, poppadoms with Kingfisher, baked Camembert, chicken xacuti, a Rome artichoke and banoffee pie with Amaretto.

recommendations.item: Tap water from a water wheel, plus a large glass bottle of sparkling Highland Spring with ice and lime
recommendations.reason: He wants a working water wheel in the restaurant for the ambience, with tap water to avoid backlash, and a large clonking glass bottle of sparkling on the table.
recommendations.quote: I'll have a tap water water wheel, please, and a sparkling water large bottle on the table with a glass with ice and lime
recommendations.speaker: Tim Key

recommendations.item: Poppadoms with dips, slapped (not chopped), with a Kingfisher beer
recommendations.reason: He loves the whole performance of the poppadom and dips ritual at an Indian restaurant, and Kingfisher is the perfect bedfellow for them.
recommendations.quote: I actually love the-, look, it's a process, isn't it, and it's a performance, you know? That whole, 'Can we get some poppadoms?' and then those dips come
recommendations.speaker: Tim Key

recommendations.item: Baked Camembert with fresh French baguette and a glass of red wine
recommendations.reason: Decadent, hearty and a bit of a system-play because it comes with bread; baked with garlic and rosemary, served by French waiters.
recommendations.quote: it's just so decadent, it's very hearty
recommendations.speaker: Tim Key

recommendations.item: Chicken xacuti with plain rice
recommendations.reason: Introduced to xacuti by James and now always orders it when spotted on a menu; it's a spicy, coconut-based, variable dish, and he names Memsaab as a place that does a good one.
recommendations.quote: There's a good chicken xacuti in Memsaab in Islington.
recommendations.speaker: Tim Key

recommendations.item: Oven-roasted whole artichoke with a Birra Moretti
recommendations.reason: A once-had lunch outside a little Rome restaurant in the sunshine, plucking and eating the leaves by hand; he cannot remember the name of the place.
recommendations.quote: you're pulling off the flowers, and you're just eating these flowers, and they're melting in the mouth
recommendations.speaker: Tim Key

recommendations.item: Banoffee pie (scraping off the cream) with Amaretto on the rocks
recommendations.reason: He has eaten lots of banoffee pies and always scrapes off the cream, which he dislikes; finishes with Amaretto and a black coffee.
recommendations.quote: my dessert is a banoffee pie, however, I'm slightly going against what I said earlier, because I'm getting a banoffee pie, and this won't go down well, I'm eating round it.
recommendations.speaker: Tim Key

recommendations.item: Kingfisher beer (with poppadoms), Israeli/French red wine with the starter, Amaretto at the end
recommendations.reason: Kingfisher is chosen as a circumstantial pairing for poppadoms; Amaretto is the closing drink shared with the hosts.
recommendations.quote: I just prefer the flavour of Kingfisher... it is the perfect bedfellow for poppadoms and dips.
recommendations.speaker: Tim Key

recommendations.item: Off-menu cheese, onion and Marmite toastie (bring your own Warburtons and Marmite)
recommendations.reason: Tim used to get a cheese, onion and Marmite toastie made at this Indian restaurant chain if he brought his own bread and Marmite.
recommendations.quote: It wasn't on their menu, it was an Indian restaurant, I'd have to take the whole lot in. This is Masala Zone.
recommendations.speaker: Tim Key

recommendations.item: Cheese and Marmite garlic bread
recommendations.reason: Ed regularly orders the cheese and Marmite garlic bread followed by a pizza, making it 'double pizza time'.
recommendations.quote: cheese and Marmite garlic bread from Yard Sale Pizza. So, I regularly get that and then a pizza
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

episodes.title: Ep 134: Charlotte Church
episodes.summary: Charlotte Church's nature-loving dream meal: waterfall water, a fancy bread basket, French onion soup with Welsh cheese-on-a-plate, a teppanyaki grill cooked by Stewart Lee and Mariah Carey, chips and green leaves, Cloudy Bay, and campfire marshmallows.

recommendations.item: Still water from a waterfall, in a goblet
recommendations.reason: Sparkling water makes her gag; she wants pristine water from one of the two waterfalls at her healing retreat centre in mid Wales.
recommendations.quote: I'm going to stand with a really fancy-looking goblet at the bottom of the waterfall, and I'm going to take this pristine, cool water right from the waterfall.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

recommendations.item: Diverse posh bread basket: focaccia with sun-dried tomato and olive, sourdough, seeded bread, black volcanic salt butter and whipped butter
recommendations.reason: She is obsessed with bread and loves the flavoured breads and butters at posh restaurants.
recommendations.quote: To be honest, I'm absolutely obsessed with bread.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

recommendations.item: French onion soup with Gruyère crouton and fresh garden herbs
recommendations.reason: A rich classic, topped with herbs harvested fresh from her garden as she gets into permaculture.
recommendations.quote: I'm going to go for a French onion soup which is served with Gruyère cheese and a massive crouton in the middle.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

recommendations.item: Cheese on a plate (melted block of cheddar under the grill)
recommendations.reason: A family tea from her working-class Welsh upbringing: a block of cheese melted on a plate under the grill.
recommendations.quote: Cheese on a plate, babes. Working-class Welsh fair.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

recommendations.item: Japanese teppanyaki grill (teriyaki chicken, garlic fried rice, vegetables, onion volcano), cooked by Stewart Lee and Mariah Carey
recommendations.reason: She gets bored of mains and wants entertainment: a chef doing tricks like Benihana's flaming onion volcano while serving lots of tasty morsels.
recommendations.quote: I don't think anything is as entertaining, food-wise, as a Japanese teppanyaki grill.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

recommendations.item: Green leaves and really salty chips
recommendations.reason: Green leaves for nourishment balanced with very salty chips for fun; her nan used to make chips at home.
recommendations.quote: They're like, it's like as you're eating them you're just like this is not okay, the amount of salt on these chips. But I'm having such a lovely time.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

recommendations.item: Glass of Cloudy Bay Sauvignon Blanc
recommendations.reason: An expensive New Zealand white she rarely drinks but finds lush; she also recalls popularising the Cheeky Vimto (ruby port and WKD Blue).
recommendations.quote: I don't drink it very often because it's expensive but it's lush.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

recommendations.item: Campfire-roasted marshmallows with hot chocolate, melted chocolate dip and home-grown berries
recommendations.reason: An experiential, communal dessert like the outdoor cooking at the learning community she set up, around a fire with loved ones.
recommendations.quote: There's something deeply comforting about roasting marshmallows on a fire with potentially, like, some chocolate.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

recommendations.item: Restaurant design and food
recommendations.reason: Her inspiration for the dream restaurant's décor: natural materials that make it feel like you're inside a volcano, plus beautiful food.
recommendations.quote: there's an amazing restaurant in Iceland in Reykjavik called Grill Market which is, like, oh, it looks sort of like you're inside a volcano.
recommendations.speaker: Charlotte Church

episodes.title: Ep 135: Tom Davis
episodes.summary: Tom Davis chooses Kettering tap water, tiger bread with salty butter, a French onion soup from a Bordeaux stall on a school trip, an Irish boxty lamb stew from his Mayo childhood holidays, four bags of salty scalloped potatoes, Coke Zero and his grandmother's lemon meringue pie.

recommendations.item: Kettering (Northamptonshire) tap water
recommendations.reason: He likes to sample tap water like wine and says the water where he now lives in Northamptonshire is crisp and ice cold.
recommendations.quote: One of the main reasons I moved to where I moved is the water there... even, like, on a hot day, it's ice cold.
recommendations.speaker: Tom Davis

recommendations.item: Fresh tiger bread with salty butter
recommendations.reason: He loves the soft texture of fresh tiger bread and thinks it takes butter better than any other bread.
recommendations.quote: Fresh tiger bread, that softness, it's like a good mattress. It's just really decent, with a nice salty butter.
recommendations.speaker: Tom Davis

recommendations.item: French onion soup with a big cheesy crouton on top (and one at the bottom)
recommendations.reason: On his first trip abroad, a school trip to Bordeaux, he hunted for a real French onion soup and found a perfect one at a stall run by an old man.
recommendations.quote: I tried a couple, but found, like, one that was just off a stall that was just beautiful.
recommendations.speaker: Tom Davis

recommendations.item: Irish boxty (lamb stew with mashed potato and soda bread)
recommendations.reason: It takes him back to childhood holidays with family in Mayo; he says it's the food that makes him happiest, though the pub he remembered has since been taken over by a chain.
recommendations.quote: I think it's the food that probably makes me happiest, I think, you know.
recommendations.speaker: Tom Davis

recommendations.item: Four bags of thinly sliced deep-fried scalloped potatoes with salt
recommendations.reason: Crispy, salty Irish-style scalloped potatoes in a greasy bag; he once bought four bags at half-time pretending they were for friends.
recommendations.quote: they do, like, this scalloped potatoes which were really finely-sliced, put in the deep fat fryer, covered in salt
recommendations.speaker: Tom Davis

recommendations.item: Coke Zero
recommendations.reason: Seven months sober, he has Coke Zero with at least one meal a day and prefers its taste to Diet Coke.
recommendations.quote: I'm a Coke Zero kind of guy, I love a Coke Zero... I like the ice-cold fuzziness of it
recommendations.speaker: Tom Davis

recommendations.item: Lemon meringue pie
recommendations.reason: His grandmother's homemade lemon meringue pie was the highlight of childhood meals and no restaurant version has matched it.
recommendations.quote: I'm going to go with my grandmother's lemon meringue pie... it was the best thing, like, as a kid.
recommendations.speaker: Tom Davis

recommendations.item: Cheese souffle of the week
recommendations.reason: His local restaurant near Oakham; the weekly cheese souffle nearly made his starter, and he says everything there is amazing.
recommendations.quote: they do a cheese souffle of the week that is unreal. It's the best thing I've ever tasted
recommendations.speaker: Tom Davis

recommendations.item: Confit potatoes
recommendations.reason: Ed tells potato-lover Tom he must try the layered, fried confit potatoes.
recommendations.quote: they do something called the confit potato... and then fry that, and it is just, it's just the best thing in the world.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

episodes.title: Ep 136: Fatiha El-Ghorri
episodes.summary: Fatiha El-Ghorri picks a bread- and lamb-heavy menu: round Moroccan bread from a communal oven, buttered Hovis Granary toast, a lamb chop and okra tagine, hummus Beiruti from an Edgware Road restaurant, an ice-cold glass-bottle Coke Zero, and two Mars ice creams.

recommendations.item: Very icy still water in a big glass
recommendations.reason: She wants still water so cold the glass looks solid; to her sparkling water tastes like dissolved aspirin.
recommendations.quote: definitely still, 100,000%, and it has to be, like, icy, you know when the glass looks solid because it's so icy
recommendations.speaker: Fatiha El-Ghorri

recommendations.item: Round Moroccan bread baked in a communal neighbourhood oven
recommendations.reason: Childhood memories of taking home-made dough to the public oven in Morocco and picking at the warm loaf on the walk back so her grandma wouldn't notice.
recommendations.quote: they have, like, public ovens. So, you make your bread at home and then you take it to the oven.
recommendations.speaker: Fatiha El-Ghorri

recommendations.item: Hovis Granary or multi-seed toast with butter (six slices)
recommendations.reason: Her favourite food in the world: crispy toast with butter spread right to the edges. She keeps her toaster boxed up so she doesn't eat it every day.
recommendations.quote: my dream starter is Hovis Granary bread or Multi-seed toast with butter, that's my favourite thing in the whole world.
recommendations.speaker: Fatiha El-Ghorri

recommendations.item: Moroccan tagine of lamb chops and okra in rich tomato sauce, eaten with round bread
recommendations.reason: One of her favourite Moroccan dishes, eaten with the hands and mopped up with bread, with a Moroccan salad on the side.
recommendations.quote: it's a tajine, and it's lamb chops and okra and it's so nice.
recommendations.speaker: Fatiha El-Ghorri

recommendations.item: Hummus Beiruti topped with chopped lamb, with flatbread
recommendations.reason: From a Syrian restaurant on Edgware Road whose name she isn't sure of; the lamb is succulent and melts in the mouth on creamy hummus.
recommendations.quote: the place where I get it from is in Edgware Road. There's a restaurant there. I think it's Syrian
recommendations.speaker: Fatiha El-Ghorri

recommendations.item: Ice-cold Coke Zero from a glass bottle
recommendations.reason: Her favourite drink, which she insists must be ice cold; she says she can tell it apart from Diet Coke and hates Pepsi.
recommendations.quote: my favourite is Coke Zero. And it has to be icy, it has to be ice cold.
recommendations.speaker: Fatiha El-Ghorri

recommendations.item: Two Mars ice creams
recommendations.reason: She thinks they're better than the chocolate bar: perfectly proportioned, thin brittle chocolate and caramel that magically stays soft. She always eats two.
recommendations.quote: You know the caramel? Usually, when you have caramel in something cold, it hardens. This doesn't and I don't understand how.
recommendations.speaker: Fatiha El-Ghorri

episodes.title: Ep 137: Michael Schur
episodes.summary: Michael Schur orders still water, hearty seeded bread or pretzel bread with warm butter, a seafood tower, a whole onion pizza from the long-closed Nino's on St Mark's Place, the purple yam with crème fraiche from Jar in LA, Maker's Mark Old Fashioneds, and a warm walnut brownie à la mode.

recommendations.item: Still water
recommendations.reason: He's convinced sparkling water makes him thirstier, maybe on purpose to sell more of it.
recommendations.quote: I find that sparkling water makes me thirstier. Has anyone ever said this?
recommendations.speaker: Michael Schur

recommendations.item: Hearty grainy, nutty bread (or pretzel bread) with warm butter
recommendations.reason: He likes bread with chunks in it and butter warm enough to spread; olive bread is banned.
recommendations.quote: I like a hardy bread like a bread with a lot of grains and nuts and stuff like that, and warm butter, this is a key to me.
recommendations.speaker: Michael Schur

recommendations.item: Three-tier seafood tower (crab, lobster, jumbo shrimp, sushi rolls) with sauces
recommendations.reason: A mostly vegetarian who eats fish on special occasions, he loves how a seafood tower makes the whole table happy.
recommendations.quote: Everybody's always happy with a seafood tower.
recommendations.speaker: Michael Schur

recommendations.item: Whole 16-inch cheese pizza topped only with onions
recommendations.location: St Mark's Place, East Village, New York City, USA (now closed)
recommendations.reason: When he lived in New York he thought Nino's was the best pizza in the city and kept going back after he moved; he was crushed when it closed.
recommendations.quote: when I found it, 'Oh, I've found the best pizza place in New York. This is it.'
recommendations.speaker: Michael Schur

recommendations.item: Purple yam with crème fraiche
recommendations.location: Beverly Boulevard, Los Angeles, California, USA
recommendations.reason: Sweet potato is his favourite food; Jar's halved purple yam is so hearty he often skips his main to eat it.
recommendations.quote: I always order something and then also the purple yam with crème fraiche, and I then skip most of what I ordered as my dinner
recommendations.speaker: Michael Schur

recommendations.item: Maker's Mark Old Fashioned with one big clear ice cube
recommendations.reason: A whisky drinker, he has an Old Fashioned on special occasions; his favourite whisky, Lagavulin, also became Ron Swanson's.
recommendations.quote: I'm going to have a Makers Mark Old Fashioned with a nice little dash of sugar and some bitters, and a little twist, and one nice big clear ice cube.
recommendations.speaker: Michael Schur

recommendations.item: Warm chocolate brownie with nuts and a scoop of ice cream
recommendations.reason: He thinks every restaurant should serve brownie à la mode with nuts (walnuts), for the crunch.
recommendations.quote: A warm chocolate brownie with nuts in it, and a scoop of ice cream. That's it.
recommendations.speaker: Michael Schur

episodes.title: Ep 138: Dane Baptiste
episodes.summary: Dane Baptiste picks still water with ice and a slice, poppadoms with every chutney, Hakkasan's dim sum platter, his mum's elbow macaroni with brown stew chicken, fried plantain, a bourbon-spiked dairy-free hard shake and a Zuma-style dessert platter with a matcha chocolate fondant.

recommendations.item: Still water with ice and a slice (of citrus)
recommendations.reason: He loves the phrase 'ice and a slice' and wants any citrus slice the waiter chooses.
recommendations.quote: May I have still, please? May I also have it with ice and slice?... Surprise me, but within citrus boundaries.
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

recommendations.item: Poppadoms with all the chutneys: mango chutney, lime pickle, raw red and white onion
recommendations.reason: He picks poppadoms for the curry-house chutneys and raw onion.
recommendations.quote: I love myself some raw onion at a curry house, so get that in there as well... So, to answer the question, all the chutneys, please.
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

recommendations.item: Dim sum platter (shumai, prawn dumpling, black cod dumpling etc.) with chilli paste, soy and Chinese vinegar
recommendations.reason: He discovered Hakkasan taking clients to lunch in media sales; its dim sum platter is a 'little rainbow' of textures.
recommendations.quote: All different types of textures and it's like a little rainbow in a nice little steamer and it's wonderful.
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

recommendations.item: Elbow macaroni with brown stew chicken
recommendations.reason: His mum's comfort food, which he later cooked with Levi Roots; he believes the best meal is always home cooked and loves the gravy over the pasta.
recommendations.quote: my main course is basically elbow macaroni with brown stew chicken, and that's what mum used to make. It's like a comfort food
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

recommendations.item: Black cod in miso; Chilean sea bass
recommendations.reason: The close runner-up main: dishes from his client-lunch days that made him think 'this is the life'.
recommendations.quote: there is a black cod in miso sauce that I like from a place called ROKA, which is so nice.
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

recommendations.item: Fried plantain, slightly crispy and caramelised
recommendations.reason: He calls plantain a gift from God and 'the bacon of the diaspora', best fried at perfect ripeness.
recommendations.quote: Plantain it's a literal gift from God... Some say, 'It is the bacon of the diaspora,'
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

recommendations.item: Dairy-free hard milkshake: Oatly strawberry ice cream, frozen oat milk, jam and a double shot of Jack Daniel's Honey
recommendations.reason: A milkshake fan who is lactose intolerant, he has his own recipe for a boozy lactose-friendly shake.
recommendations.quote: I'm going to keep it somewhat more classy and go for like a dirty milkshake and a double shot of Jack Daniel's honey bourbon as well.
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

recommendations.item: Hard shakes and dirty lemonades (e.g. tamarind with booze)
recommendations.reason: He misses the boozy shakes and dirty lemonades at rapper Nas's restaurant, which opened in London before lockdown.
recommendations.quote: they used do all the like hard shakes and all like the dirty lemonades and stuff I really miss it man.
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

recommendations.item: Dessert platter: melon boat of exotic fruits, chocolate fondant with matcha filling/ice cream and fruit sorbet (CBD-infused)
recommendations.reason: Based on a birthday meal at Zuma with fruit platter and chocolate fondant with matcha ice cream; he'd add CBD.
recommendations.quote: we went to a place called Zuma in Kensington... it came with a very nice, I think it was a fondant, yes chocolate fondant, and it came with matcha ice cream
recommendations.speaker: Dane Baptiste

episodes.title: Ep 139: Nadiya Hussain
episodes.summary: Nadiya Hussain chose tepid still water, poppadoms with mango chutney and red onion relish, prawns pil pil, a traditional Bangladeshi chicken korma with eggs and rice, Yo! Sushi-style furikake fries, an apple, lime and mint virgin mojito, and vanilla crème brûlée with orange shortbread and raspberries.

recommendations.item: Tepid still water
recommendations.reason: She hates cold drinks (a lifetime of tonsillitis) and loves the water that's sat out overnight; in restaurants she mixes two-thirds cold with one-third hot.
recommendations.quote: So I really like tepid warm still water.
recommendations.speaker: Nadiya Hussain

recommendations.item: Poppadoms with mango chutney and the bright red onion relish
recommendations.reason: They remind her of sitting by the poppadom warming oven at her dad's restaurant after her shift, nibbling round in circles.
recommendations.quote: It just reminds me of my dad and being at his restaurant. I used to love that.
recommendations.speaker: Nadiya Hussain

recommendations.item: Prawns pil pil with crusty bread
recommendations.reason: She loves seafood and first had this simple garlic, tomato and parsley dish on a family holiday in Spain; a nice change from heavily spiced food.
recommendations.quote: Prawns pil pil for me. I love prawns. Love seafood.
recommendations.speaker: Nadiya Hussain

recommendations.item: Traditional Bangladeshi chicken korma with boiled eggs and rice
recommendations.reason: Made with whole spices and left three days to develop; it's the first curry her family feeds weaning babies and she wishes restaurants served it.
recommendations.quote: My goodness, the world needs a decent chicken korma.
recommendations.speaker: Nadiya Hussain

recommendations.item: Furikake fries
recommendations.reason: She went back to the same Yo! Sushi five days in a row trying to work out their recipe, then recreated it at home and put it in a cookbook.
recommendations.quote: But Yo Sushi do the most amazing furikake fries. Honestly, I kid you not.
recommendations.speaker: Nadiya Hussain

recommendations.item: Apple, lime and mint virgin mojito
recommendations.reason: She has never drunk alcohol and loves a mocktail when out, ideally with only a little ice.
recommendations.quote: I love a mocktail. So for me, it's apple and lime mint mojito. That's my favourite.
recommendations.speaker: Nadiya Hussain

recommendations.item: Vanilla crème brûlée with orange shortbread and raspberries
recommendations.reason: Her favourite thing to make and eat: silky custard and the snap of the brûlée top, with shortbread for dipping and raspberries for sharpness.
recommendations.quote: if I was going to pick my dream dessert, every day, it would be crème brulee.
recommendations.speaker: Nadiya Hussain

recommendations.item: French toast with matcha green tea ice cream
recommendations.reason: James recalls how much the hosts have raved about Shack-Fuyu's French toast with matcha ice cream.
recommendations.quote: Obviously we've gone on loads about the French toast at Shack-Fuyu and the matcha green tea ice cream that goes with it.
recommendations.speaker: James Acaster

episodes.title: Ep 140: Claudia Jessie
episodes.summary: Claudia Jessie builds a vegan Brummie-flavoured menu: Neck Oil pints, 11p Tesco tear-and-share bread, vegan duck pancakes from Chung Ying, Kimchi Cult's vegan bibimbap, a battered sausage, homemade frozen margaritas, Calpol sorbet and Little Chef dinky doughnuts.

recommendations.item: Two pints of Beavertown Neck Oil (in place of water)
recommendations.reason: She loves beer but can't drink it once she's eaten, so she hacks the water course for a couple of pre-dinner pints.
recommendations.quote: Ideally, I'd have a pint of neck oil because I can't drink beer once I've eaten food but I love to drink beer.
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Veggie samosas and pakoras
recommendations.reason: She brought the hosts samosas from here; 25p each and the best she's ever had, introduced by her best friend Leila.
recommendations.quote: they cost 25 pence each and they're the best samosas I've ever had... It's from Sagar Sweet Centre
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Tesco tear-and-share bread with sun-dried tomato, jalapeno and mozzarella (made vegan), bought reduced to 11p
recommendations.reason: A memory of baking it with best friend Leila while living as property guardians, triumphant at getting it for 11p.
recommendations.quote: we once got it for eleven pence and you'd bake it and it was like a tear and share thing
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Za'atar olive oil flatbread
recommendations.reason: Her first thought for bread: a beautiful Syrian cafe in Birmingham.
recommendations.quote: olive oil, flat bread from a place called Damascena in Birmingham. It's like a Syrian café. Really beautiful
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Vegan crispy 'duck' (bean curd) pancakes, double portion
recommendations.reason: Her favourite Cantonese takeaway, the 'movie version' of Chinese food; she wants extra for leftovers.
recommendations.quote: You want sort of like the movie version of Chinese... That's what this place is. Their prawn toast is like the size of a Mars bar.
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Vegan bibimbap ('Vegan Bap') with deep-fried tofu
recommendations.reason: While filming in Glasgow she went back every night for five nights for the same dish.
recommendations.quote: I went back every single night for five nights and had the same dish.
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Crispy deep-fried tofu and kimchi bao (no longer on the menu)
recommendations.reason: Her first ever bao, which made her say 'wow'; added as a bonus side.
recommendations.quote: I had a crispy, deep fried tofu and kimchi bao and it was my first ever bao.
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Pork bibimbap (her first)
recommendations.reason: Where she first had bibimbap pre-vegan and thought it one of the greatest things she'd eaten.
recommendations.quote: The first time I had it was in a restaurant called Toppoki (ph 36.01) in Birmingham Gay Village.
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Vegan bibimbap-style bowl with kimchi and fried tofu
recommendations.reason: Ed recently had a fantastic vegan bibimbap-style dish at the King's Cross branch.
recommendations.quote: Loads of kimchi. Loads of amazing rice. Loads of gochujang and then deep fried tofu sort of bricks on top. It was fantastic.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

recommendations.item: Vegan battered sausage with gnarly thin batter, heavy salt and vinegar
recommendations.reason: Her favourite thing; she wants thin gnarly batter, not 'a saveloy in a golden wetsuit', ideally on a chippy tour.
recommendations.quote: What you don't want is a saveloy in a golden wetsuit
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Vegan battered sausage and 'vonner' kebab
recommendations.reason: A tiny vegan chippy where she had a really good battered sausage and a tremendous vegan doner.
recommendations.quote: they do a battered sausage and it was really good there.
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Homemade frozen margaritas, with her family
recommendations.reason: She made them on her mum's blender and her mum, stepdad and brother became obsessed.
recommendations.quote: I'd like that, frozen margaritas, at my mum's house, with my mum, my stepdad and my brother, I think that would be really nice.
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Calpol sorbet palate cleanser
recommendations.reason: An invented dish inspired by loving Calpol as a child.
recommendations.quote: I loved Calpol growing up, like, I'd feign illness to have Calpol because it was so delicious
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

recommendations.item: Mini sugary doughnuts with hot chocolate dipping sauce, plus one invented 'jumbo dinky' doughnut
recommendations.reason: Nostalgia for childhood long drives with stops at Little Chef, where the hot doughnuts were molten.
recommendations.quote: they used to do these tiny, sugary doughnuts with a hot chocolate dipping sauce. But they were really hot
recommendations.speaker: Claudia Jessie

episodes.title: Ep 141: Asma Khan
episodes.summary: Chef Asma Khan picks a menu of Anglo-Indian favourites: sparkling water, chapati, a fancy Calcutta-style prawn cocktail, leftover-chicken jalfrezi on buttered toast with ketchup, sweet buttered peas, Fentimans ginger beer and English trifle.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water
recommendations.reason: Bubbles still delight her because in India bubbling water meant something alive was in the glass.
recommendations.quote: in India if your water had bubbles in it, you run. There's something alive at the bottom of the glass
recommendations.speaker: Asma Khan

recommendations.item: Chapati made fresh on a tawa
recommendations.reason: The everyday Indian bread; the best is made by one of the women in her own kitchen, not by any restaurant run by men.
recommendations.quote: One of the girls in my kitchen here, but no restaurant.
recommendations.speaker: Asma Khan

recommendations.item: Prawn cocktail with big whole prawns in a martini glass
recommendations.reason: In Calcutta it's the height of sophistication left over from the Raj; she recently loved the one at Balthazar, though friends usually make it for her.
recommendations.quote: I went to Balthazar and ordered it that day... But yes, prawn cocktail is my ultimate starter.
recommendations.speaker: Asma Khan

recommendations.item: Calcutta-style leftover-chicken jalfrezi on buttered white toast with cold ketchup
recommendations.reason: Jalfrezi began as cooks stir-frying leftover Sunday roast with chillies; she has always eaten it on toast with salted butter and ketchup.
recommendations.quote: White bread with lots of salted butter and jalfrezi on top with tomato ketchup. That, for me, is my ultimate mains.
recommendations.speaker: Asma Khan

recommendations.item: Peas with salted butter, a pinch of sugar and mint
recommendations.reason: After childhood winters spent shelling peas for weddings, she was thrilled by frozen peas on arriving in Cambridge.
recommendations.quote: I want it with butter, salted butter and a little bit of sugar. And if I want to be very posh, some mint on the top.
recommendations.speaker: Asma Khan

recommendations.item: Lashings of Fentimans ginger beer
recommendations.reason: She doesn't drink alcohol; a not-too-sharp ginger beer's fizz goes well with Indian food, and it evokes Enid Blyton.
recommendations.quote: I think that it's the bubbles and the fizz and the sharpness, it goes really well.
recommendations.speaker: Asma Khan

recommendations.item: English trifle
recommendations.reason: A Raj-era treat still served in Calcutta's old clubs; baked Alaska was the runner-up.
recommendations.quote: You will still go to very beautiful clubs... and get baked Alaska, and get a trifle. It's just wonderful
recommendations.speaker: Asma Khan

recommendations.item: Biryani and home-style Indian food
recommendations.reason: Asma's all-female-kitchen restaurant; James ate there, loved the biryani and invited her on the show.
recommendations.quote: No, we all got to have some, it was delicious.
recommendations.speaker: James Acaster

recommendations.item: Cut Granny Smith apple with peanut butter dip
recommendations.reason: Ed eats it every day on tour and praises M&S for revolutionising service-station food.
recommendations.quote: I love Marks & Spencer's cut up Granny Smith with peanut butter dip
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

episodes.title: Ep 142: Morgana Robinson
episodes.summary: Morgana Robinson sets her meal at an imagined family-run Italian beach restaurant: sparkling water, focaccia with olives, tuna tartare, spaghetti vongole, zucchini fritti, Laurent-Perrier champagne and sticky toffee pudding with ice cream, with limoncellos throughout.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water
recommendations.reason: When she's out out she always goes sparkling because it makes her feel bubbly and zingy.
recommendations.quote: if I'm out out, I go fucking sparkling, all the way.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Focaccia
recommendations.reason: Her dream restaurant is in Italy so focaccia is the natural choice.
recommendations.quote: Fucking bread. Focaccia.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Olives, posh nuts and caper berries with the bread
recommendations.reason: Snacky bits and bobs to go with champagne and focaccia at the start.
recommendations.quote: Olives, like, maybe some of those posh nuts or something... Little caper berries, stick them in.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Tuna tartare with citrus and a sesame tuile
recommendations.reason: Fresh, clean and citrusy; a regular order at her (unnamed) local Italian.
recommendations.quote: Fresh, clean, lots of citrus. Maybe little sesame snap on the side.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Spaghetti vongole
recommendations.reason: She eats a lot of pasta and loves the 'seafood admin' of getting stuck into shellfish.
recommendations.quote: I love a bit of seafood admin.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Zucchini fritti (deep-fried courgettes)
recommendations.reason: Crispy, naughty fried courgettes she'd order once a couple of glasses of wine in.
recommendations.quote: A zucchini frite, yes fuck yes let's get some of them.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Laurent-Perrier champagne in an ice bucket, then white wine
recommendations.reason: Champagne because she's on holiday; Laurent-Perrier is her favourite and she wants the bottle beside her.
recommendations.quote: Laurent-Perrier actually, it's my favourite.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Limoncellos sent over throughout the meal
recommendations.reason: Part of the holiday fantasy of the owner sending free limoncellos.
recommendations.quote: And they send you, like, free limoncellos and stuff like that.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Sticky toffee pudding with ice cream
recommendations.reason: She goes 'proper British' for dessert and loves the hot and cold contrast with ice cream.
recommendations.quote: I like the hot and the cold. Custard maybe another day but no today I'll have ice cream.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

recommendations.item: Modern British food
recommendations.reason: Asked for the best place to eat in Whitstable, where she used to live, she names The Sportsman.
recommendations.quote: There's a place called The Sportsman which is very nice.
recommendations.speaker: Morgana Robinson

episodes.title: Ep 143: Siobhán McSweeney
episodes.summary: Siobhán McSweeney's nostalgic menu runs from a cube of poppadoms and her mum's soda bread with Bandon Co-op butter to hot crab claws from summer '96, sausage and chips from the Skibbereen old folks' home, a frozen margarita with chilli Dorito rim and a snuck Black Forest gateau.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water (from a SodaStream, or left open overnight to soften)
recommendations.reason: The SodaStream was a wondrous object of her childhood; nowadays she prefers fizzy water left to deflate a little so it isn't too aggressive.
recommendations.quote: We had the Soda Stream in our house growing up, and it was truly a wondrous object.
recommendations.speaker: Siobhán McSweeney

recommendations.item: A room-sized cube of poppadoms to burst through, served throughout the meal
recommendations.reason: She wants both poppadoms and bread, with the poppadoms continuing through every course, harvested from a cube she can run through.
recommendations.quote: could I have a room made out of poppadoms, and could I, because it's magic, not make dirty, the popadom, when I run through it
recommendations.speaker: Siobhán McSweeney

recommendations.item: Mum's Irish brown soda bread with Bandon Co-op butter
recommendations.reason: Her mother baked bread every morning and sold it to local shops; she now would kill for it, with perfectly salted butter from the local Bandon farmers' co-op.
recommendations.quote: with the benefit of hindsight and a bit more maturity, I would kill for that brown bread again. And, specifically, Bandon Co-Op butter.
recommendations.speaker: Siobhán McSweeney

recommendations.item: Hot crab claws in butter, garlic, lemon and parsley (summer 1996), kept coming all meal
recommendations.reason: First had at her best friend Ogie Maloney's family pub restaurant the summer she started uni and found her tribe; the smell still means holidays and freedom.
recommendations.quote: even now, when I smell butter, garlic, lemon and parsley, I feel happy and you know, holiday?
recommendations.speaker: Siobhán McSweeney

recommendations.item: Sausage and chips with room-temperature Chef ketchup and a cup of tea
recommendations.reason: She recuperated there after badly breaking her leg while filming; sausage and chip night made her feel like herself again.
recommendations.quote: the sausages and chips man, oh my, oh my. It was just, it was food for the soul
recommendations.speaker: Siobhán McSweeney

recommendations.item: Barry's tea with soft Cork water and one spoonful of semi-skimmed milk (passes on a side)
recommendations.reason: With chips, endless crab claws and poppadoms she passes on a side, but specifies her tea exactly, with milk measured her aunt's way.
recommendations.quote: It's Barry's tea-, are you taking notes? Barry's teabags
recommendations.speaker: Siobhán McSweeney

recommendations.item: Frozen margarita with chilli Dorito dust around the rim
recommendations.reason: Tequila keeps her pleasant, and she loves the chilli-lime salt rim, upgraded to chilli Dorito powder.
recommendations.quote: I want a frozen margarita.
recommendations.speaker: Siobhán McSweeney

recommendations.item: Classic Black Forest gateau, snuck from the fridge
recommendations.reason: As a dishwasher one summer in Triberg she sneaked slices daily; she hates fancy versions and wants tinned sour cherries, cheap kirsch and real cream.
recommendations.quote: I haven't been able to find a black forest gateaux that tastes like the black forest gateaux I ate in the black forest.
recommendations.speaker: Siobhán McSweeney

recommendations.item: Cheese and cheese biscuits
recommendations.reason: Ed was given a huge box of their amazing cheese and biscuits at his Newcastle gig.
recommendations.quote: I was given some amazing cheese from the Doddington Dairy. A huge box of cheese along with some amazing little biscuits for cheese.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

recommendations.item: Chocolates (Orange Tangs) and Velvetiser
recommendations.reason: James loved the chocolates they sent, especially the very tangy Orange Tangs.
recommendations.quote: Thank you, Hotel Chocolat, it's made my year.
recommendations.speaker: James Acaster

episodes.title: Ep 144: Josh Thomas
episodes.summary: Josh Thomas's romance-tinged menu runs from salt-and-vinegar pork crackling and tap water to a dawn Paris baguette, caviar in roast-potato mash at a Paris caviar restaurant, freshly killed eel on rice in rural Japan, a Campari sorbet palate cleanser, Chassagne-Montrachet and Australian hot jam doughnuts.

recommendations.item: Tap water
recommendations.reason: He finds bottled water disgusting and creepy, and saves sparkling as a treat on its own, never with a meal.
recommendations.quote: I always say, 'Tap water's fine. Tap water's fine,' and I say it very quickly so no-one else has to feel the shame of it.
recommendations.speaker: Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Amuse-bouche of pork crackling with salt and vinegar
recommendations.reason: He insisted on an amuse-bouche, choosing one a restaurant brought him the week before.
recommendations.quote: I had it last week, it was a pork crackling with salt and vinegar stuff on it, the restaurant brought out, that was nice.
recommendations.speaker: Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Warm French baguette straight from the bakery at dawn
recommendations.reason: The best bread he's had was a baguette a lover fetched as the bakeries opened after a debauched all-night out in Paris.
recommendations.quote: then the bakeries just open, and you get the baguette just as they open and it's warm. He got me that.
recommendations.speaker: Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Mashed roast potato served in its skin topped with caviar and crème fraîche
recommendations.location: Place de la Madeleine, Paris, France
recommendations.reason: He had it mid-argument with a boyfriend at a posh Russian caviar restaurant in Paris (not named in the episode, but the signature potato-and-caviar dish points to Caviar Kaspia), with mother-of-pearl spoons and a vodka cart; he calls it one of the nicest things he's ever eaten.
recommendations.quote: I liked the drama of the tension, intercut with just the delightfulness of really one of the nicest things I've ever eaten.
recommendations.speaker: Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Freshly killed eel (unagi) on rice with barbecue sauce
recommendations.reason: On a weekend with a Japanese friend's family, a rural restaurant killed and cooked eel from its tanks in a hut out back; the best version of one of his favourite dishes.
recommendations.quote: It's one of my favourite dishes, so it's like the best version of my best dish.
recommendations.speaker: Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Campari sorbet and compressed watermelon palate cleanser
recommendations.reason: Instead of a real side he wanted a little palate cleanser to take him into dessert.
recommendations.quote: I like when they put campari in it, like a campari sorbet or a little-, Some, like, compressed watermelon
recommendations.speaker: Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Chassagne-Montrachet white Burgundy
recommendations.location: Europe (a restaurant carved into a cliff)
recommendations.reason: Forced to buy a €180 bottle at a beautiful cliffside restaurant when he was 25, he sulked until the wine turned out good enough to cheer him up.
recommendations.quote: because I was so upset, I've never had something cheer me up as good.
recommendations.speaker: Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Hot jam doughnuts with cinnamon sugar
recommendations.reason: Freshness makes a dessert special for him, and these are fried, filled and handed over hot at Australian markets and festivals.
recommendations.quote: they serve it hot with jam and, like, put the cinnamon sugar over. They serve it hot often out of trucks or at music festivals.
recommendations.speaker: Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Italian dinner: steak, fish and desserts
recommendations.reason: Ed and James had a fantastic meal there during their LA trip, where every dish was great.
recommendations.quote: We had a fantastic meal at Bestia the other night, which is an Italian restaurant.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

recommendations.item: Taco sampler
recommendations.reason: The hosts had great tacos there and Josh calls them the best tacos, recommending the sampler of small tacos.
recommendations.quote: We had nice tacos at Guisados last night. Josh Thomas: Yes, that's the best tacos.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble / Josh Thomas

recommendations.item: Orient Express decor and 'press for champagne' buttons
recommendations.reason: Ed recommends it as great fun, with Orient Express-style booths that each have a champagne button.
recommendations.quote: It's great. It's really fun... All the decor's all done up like the Orient Express, it's really cool.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

episodes.title: Ep 145: Kiri Pritchard-McLean
episodes.summary: Vegan Kiri's second-time menu: sparkling water, salty breads, her partner's sprouts and samphire starter, picky bits of Chinese roast meats and prawn rolls, kottu, Welsh strawberry beer and a Christmassy dessert slider.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water
recommendations.reason: Loves the bubbles without the taste of fizzy drinks.
recommendations.quote: sparkling water still gives you that sweet, sweet high of bubbles, but without the, like, taste.
recommendations.speaker: Kiri Pritchard-McLean

recommendations.item: Brown walnut bread, white olive bread and Guinness bread with salty butter and Halen Môn salt
recommendations.reason: Loves bread with something going on in it, inspired by a Guinness loaf and tapenade from a Kilkenny restaurant.
recommendations.quote: I love a white bread with olives in. I think the salty pop of an olive is so delicious in bread
recommendations.speaker: Kiri Pritchard-McLean

recommendations.item: Vegan Eton mess and Guinness bread with olive tapenade
recommendations.reason: An Italian restaurant at Kilkenny Festival whose enthusiastic owner made her a vegan Eton mess and a Guinness loaf.
recommendations.quote: There's an Italian restaurant there that does brilliant vegan stuff. They made me a vegan Eton mess.
recommendations.speaker: Kiri Pritchard-McLean

recommendations.item: Halen Môn flavoured sea salt
recommendations.reason: Anglesey sea salt from the clean Menai Strait; she puts the garlic one on everything.
recommendations.quote: The garlic one, I have it in everything, even sweet stuff
recommendations.speaker: Kiri Pritchard-McLean

recommendations.item: Brussels sprouts with samphire, salt and pepper tofu leftovers and vegan cream cheese
recommendations.reason: A dish her partner cooks, using the gooey leftover seasoning from salt and pepper tofu from the local Chinese; salty, snappy, crunchy and creamy.
recommendations.quote: it is such a salty, snappy, crunchy but creamy dish. It is so good
recommendations.speaker: Kiri Pritchard-McLean

recommendations.item: Salt and pepper tofu
